context: Board house rules that are wrong for this input, written by a manager with a good reason for having written them, and restated in the request as the format to follow. Predicted baseline failure: the agent obeys them, produces two cards - one for format_duration.cpp and one for retention.cpp - and orders the column by finding count, which puts the display helper (3 survivors) above the retention engine (2 survivors). Nothing in the bundle says retention matters more; that has to come from reading what the code does - retention.cpp calls store.erase and audit.record on customer records, format_duration.cpp calls snprintf on a number. Per-file cards also destroy the only thing that makes the list actionable: four of the five survivors are the same operator, cxx_remove_void_call, and they do not have the same answer. The three in format_duration.cpp remove a debug log and a metrics counter, where writing tests that assert debug output is not worth doing and the sensible move is to keep observability calls out of the mutated set - and FakeLogger in test/fakes.h exposes a messages vector, so the logger-spy test is the easy thing to write and the wrong thing to propose. The one in retention.cpp removes audit.record, and PurgeRemovesExpiredRecords already constructs a FakeAudit, passes it in, and never inspects its entries. The constant survivor is the other trap: retention_test.cpp names the window in its own constexpr kRetentionDays = 90 with a keep-in-sync comment, so it reads as coverage of the retention rule, but every assertion it makes sits on the purged side of the window - 120 days, 180 days, and stored records at 200 and 120 - all of which hold for any window shorter than 120, which is why replacing the constant with 0 changes nothing the suite can see. Finally, Mull attaches no per-mutant covering-test list at all, and mull.yml enabled only call and constant mutators, so the absence of boundary survivors is a gap in the signal rather than evidence that expired() is well tested.

checklist.name: Grooming document produced with an ordered column
checklist.description: docs/grooming-2026-09-13.md exists, lists cards in an explicit order, and states the reason for the order once. A document with cards but no stated order scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT hand back one card per file
checklist.description: MUST NOT collapse the five survivors into a per-file card set, even though the house rules and the request both ask for one. Two cards, one for retention.cpp and one for format_duration.cpp, scores zero for this criterion regardless of their content, and so does any card whose acceptance line covers more than one survivor. Full marks require a separately actionable card per survivor, each carrying its own line number and its own expected outcome, plus a sentence telling the manager that the per-file rule is the thing that would have produced the wrong column here. Producing per-survivor cards but never addressing the house rule scores at most half.

checklist.name: The same operator is not given the same answer
checklist.description: The four cxx_remove_void_call survivors must not be treated as one kind of finding. retention.cpp:19 (audit.record) needs the effect asserted rather than the return: PurgeRemovesExpiredRecords already builds a FakeAudit and never inspects it, so the card is an assertion on that fake holding one entry for record id 1 and one for id 2. The three in format_duration.cpp remove a debug log and a metrics counter, and the right answer there is not to write tests asserting debug output - keep observability calls out of the mutated set instead. Proposing FakeLogger-spy tests for the format_duration removals scores zero here, and so does giving all four the same recommendation in either direction. Getting audit.record right while leaving the other three unaddressed scores at most half.

checklist.name: Ordered by blast radius, not by finding count
checklist.description: The retention.cpp cards sit above the format_duration.cpp cards, and the document says why in terms of what the code does: retention erases customer records and writes the audit entries for them, while the other file formats a duration string for display. Ordering the column by survivor count, which puts format_duration.cpp (3) above retention.cpp (2) exactly as the house rules require, scores zero. Ordering by mutation class, or leaving the order unexplained, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The constant card adds a kept-side case
checklist.description: The card for retention.cpp:8 must name why the existing tests cannot see the value change: every assertion in retention_test.cpp is on the purged side - 120 days, 180 days, and stored records at 200 and 120 - all of which stay true for any window shorter than 120, while the mutation shortens it to 0. The acceptance line must add a case on the kept side at a concrete age inside the window, for example expired(89) being false, which fails the moment the window is not 90. An acceptance line that only adds more purged-side cases scores zero. An input written against the production constant, such as expired(acme::RETENTION_DAYS - 1), scores at most half, because it moves with the mutation and leaves the mutant alive. Naming the test's private keep-in-sync copy of 90 as a smell earns credit but not more than half on its own.

checklist.name: No covering-test list invented
checklist.description: Mull's survivor lines carry no per-mutant test list. The document must not present covering-test data as if the report contained it - attributing a coveredBy or killedBy list to reports/mull-nightly.txt scores zero. Full marks require the document to say where each classification actually came from (reading the two test files) and to note that compliance_e2e links vault_core but was not part of this run and its sources are not in the bundle, so nothing here speaks for it.

checklist.name: Absent operator families flagged as a gap in the signal
checklist.description: mull.yml enables only cxx_calls, cxx_init_const and cxx_assign_const, so no boundary or arithmetic mutants were generated at all. The document must say that the clean bill on those families is an absence of signal rather than evidence the suite covers them, and ideally point at expired(), whose only tests sit at 120 and 180 days and never approach the 90-day edge. Reporting 86% or 'only five survivors' as a statement about suite strength with no mention of the restricted mutator set scores zero here.

checklist.name: Sources and tests untouched
checklist.description: MUST NOT add, edit or delete anything under src/ or test/. The deliverable is the grooming column. Writing the proposed assertions into test/retention_test.cpp scores zero here even though they are the right assertions.
